## Hohmann transfer

The cheapest two-burn move between circular orbits of radius $r_1$ and $r_2$. The first burn raises the far point of the orbit to $r_2$:

$$
\Delta v_1 = \sqrt{\frac{\mu}{r_1}}\left(\sqrt{\frac{2r_2}{r_1+r_2}}-1\right)
$$

Here $\mu = GM$ is the standard gravitational parameter of the central body.

The total cost is Δv = Δv₁ + Δv₂.

pages.markdown:
## The second burn

At $r_2$ the craft is slower than a circular orbit there, so it burns again:

$$
\Delta v_2 = \sqrt{\frac{\mu}{r_2}}\left(1-\sqrt{\frac{2r_1}{r_1+r_2}}\right)
$$

The total cost is $\Delta v = \Delta v_1 + \Delta v_2$.

pages.markdown:
## Transfer time

The transfer is half an ellipse with semi-major axis $a = \frac{r_1 + r_2}{2}$, so by Kepler's third law:

$$
t_H = \pi\sqrt{\frac{(r_1+r_2)^3}{8\mu}}
$$
